chunks: A number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Abbas ibn A'mir, from Abdallah ibn Bukayr, from his father, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: If you are certain that you have broken your Wudu, then renew it, and beware of ever renewing the Wudu unless you are certain that you have broken it.
ai.seo_question: When should one renew their Wudu according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) instructs that one should only renew their ritual ablution (Wudu) when they are certain that it has been broken, cautioning against renewing it prematurely or without certainty. This hadith establishes the principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) in fiqh, where the default state of purity remains until definitive proof of its nullification arises, thereby preventing unnecessary ritual burden (*tashaddud*).

en.ammaar-muslim: 5. [5/98] al-Kafi: A number of our companions from Ahmad b. Muhammad from al-Abbas b. A’mir from Abdallah b. Bukayr from his father who said:
Abu Abdillah عليه السلام said to me: if you are sure that you have broken your Wudhu then renew it, beware of ever renewing a Wudhu unless you are certain that you have broken it.
